banner: SPECULATIVE OUTPUT — no verified decipherment of the Voynich Manuscript exists. This is model output under a stated hypothesis, not a reading of the manuscript.

findings.implication: A ceiling, not evidence. The pipeline recovers a key it is given, which is why a confident-looking rendering proves nothing on its own.
findings.metric: H1 gloss accuracy on ciphertext we built

findings.implication: Held-out and training pages are indistinguishable, which is what a dictionary-matching pipeline looks like — it is not evidence of generalisation.
Where the two transcriptions disagree, so do the glosses, four times out of five. The reading is a property of the transcription, not of the manuscript.
findings.metric: gloss agreement on tokens whose ZL and IT surfaces differ

findings.implication: Consistency is guaranteed by context-free glossing, so it is not evidence. The collapse ratio it hides is: the rendering is heavily many-to-one.
findings.metric: Voynich types per distinct English word (gated view)

findings.implication: Page topic and glossed vocabulary vary together beyond chance, and pseudo-Voynich under the same page labels does not.
The rendering is no more English-like in its word order than the same words in random order, and both are far from real English.
findings.metric: bits/word of the rendering under a douay_rheims bigram model

findings.implication: Blocked by the three open §5.1 gaps; no anchor evidence exists either way.

Text that encodes nothing renders at least as well as the manuscript. Under the criterion the plan fixed in advance, the pipeline is a fluency generator and its Voynich output carries no evidential weight.
findings.metric: `grille` gated coverage as a share of the manuscript's
findings.null: 1.00 means gibberish renders as well; 5 draws span 103%–122%

findings.implication: The pipeline does distinguish the manuscript from character noise, which sounds better than it is: §7.2.1's `grille` clears the same bar and then renders more than the manuscript. Reordering whole words, meanwhile, changes nothing at all, because no stage of the pipeline reads a sequence.
findings.metric: character-shuffled Voynichese, gated coverage as a share of the manuscript's
findings.null: word-order shuffle scores 0.978 — a tautology, not a test

findings.implication: Unrelated plaintext languages produce comparable Latin gloss rates, so the method does not identify the language and the glosses are not evidence for one.
findings.metric: spread in gated coverage across plaintext languages

findings.implication: Re-running the same search with a different seed changes a large share of the reading, so the key is not identified and no individual gloss is stable.
findings.metric: mean token-level gloss agreement across independent re-searches
findings.null: 1.00 would mean the key is identified

findings.implication: The headline coverage depends heavily on choices — tokenization above all — that no evidence fixes.
findings.metric: largest swing in gated coverage across analysis choices

findings.implication: Every listed zone is enumerated with its row count, so no reader has to infer which parts of the rendering are least supported.
findings.metric: weakest zone: tokens containing a unit the key never saw

findings.implication: Stated at the top of every report and broken out per stratum, so a complete-looking speculative rendering cannot be mistaken for complete coverage.
